data.name: Lukas
data.gender_notes: Lukas is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Roman family name Lucanus, meaning from Lucania, a region in southern Italy. In the New Testament, Luke was a physician and a companion of Paul, who authored the third gospel and the Acts of the Apostles. The name Lukas carries the meaning “Man from Lucania” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Lukas usually hope their child will grow to embody man from lucania and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of compassionate and loyal friendship in the Christian tradition.
data.etymology: Lukas belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Man from Lucania.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Lukas total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

in_hebrew.name: לוקאס

in_greek.name: Λουκάς
in_greek.long_meaning: το όνομα Λουκάς είναι ελληνικής προέλευσης και σημαίνει ο θεός είναι λυτρωτής, και προέρχεται από την ελληνική λέξη λύω που σημαίνει λυτρώσω, ο Λουκάς ήταν ένας από τους ευαγγελιστές και φίλος του αποστόλου Παύλου, και έγραψε το κατά Λουκάν ευαγγέλιο

in_latin.name: Lucas
in_latin.long_meaning: nomen Lucas latinum est, quod significat deo liberator, et derivatur a verbo lucare, quod significat liberare, Lucas fuit evangelista et amicus apostoli Pauli, et scripsit evangelium secundum Lucam

in_english.name: Lukas
in_english.long_meaning: the name Lukas is of Greek origin, meaning God is liberator, derived from the Greek word lyo, meaning to liberate, Lukas was a companion of the apostle Paul and wrote the Gospel of Luke, symbolizing spiritual freedom and salvation

data.cultural_impact: The name Lukas appears in the New Testament and has been in use since ancient times. It has a rich cultural heritage, particularly in Europe, where it has been a popular given name for centuries. In some parts of Europe, Lukas is still a common name, and it is considered to be a strong and noble name.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christian tradition, Luke is celebrated as a patron saint of artists, doctors, and travelers. As a patron saint of artists, Luke is believed to have inspired and protected those who create beautiful works of art. As a patron saint of doctors, he is prayed to for protection and guidance in the medical profession. And as a patron saint of travelers, he is invoked for safe and prosperous journeys. The spiritual name Lukas carries with it the blessings of creativity, healing, and safe travel.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Lukas, derived from the Latin name Lucius, means "bringer of light." In the New Testament, Saint Luke is known as the "Evangelist of the Gentiles," whose Gospel and Acts of the Apostles illuminated the path of Christianity to the non-Jewish world.

historical_references.reference: Lukas is a name of Latin origin, derived from the Greek name Loukas, which is itself derived from the name of the Evangelist Luke.
historical_references.context: Lukas was a popular name among the nobility and clergy in medieval Europe.

trends: In recent years, the name Lukas has seen a resurgence in popularity, particularly in Germany and other European countries
